item.research_question: How does compositional heterogeneity affect the mechanical properties of high-entropy alloy nanoparticles?
item.processing_route: Fast Moving Bed Pyrolysis (FMBP) strategy, with a heating rate of 10 K·min−1 and annealing at 923 K for 120 min
item.test_conditions: In situ compression testing in a transmission electron microscope (TEM) with a displacement control rate of 2 nm·s−1
key_findings: The yield strength of HEA nanoparticles exhibits a transition from a “smaller-is-stronger” to a “smaller-is-weaker” phenomenon below a critical size of ~180 nm
The deformation mode changes from homogeneous to heterogeneous with decreasing particle size
The work-hardening ability deteriorates significantly below the critical size
The compositional heterogeneity leads to a variation in local stacking-fault energy (SFE) and lattice friction
The critical size for the transition is influenced by the spatial correlation length of compositional heterogeneity
item.mechanism: The compositional heterogeneity 'roughens' the landscape for dislocation motion, leading to a variation in local SFE and lattice friction, which in turn affects the mechanical properties
item.limitations: The experimental results are limited to a specific alloy composition and processing route
item.future_work: Further studies are needed to explore the effect of compositional heterogeneity on the mechanical properties of HEAs with different alloy compositions and processing routes
quotes: compositional heterogeneity plays an important role in affecting the mechanical properties of HEAs

records.text: Paper card. Question: How does compositional heterogeneity affect the mechanical properties of high-entropy alloy nanoparticles?. System: Fe18Co16Ni8Cu20Pd12.5Ir1.5Pt10Au14 nanoparticles. Processing: Fast Moving Bed Pyrolysis (FMBP) strategy, with a heating rate of 10 K·min−1 and annealing at 923 K for 120 min. Test conditions: In situ compression testing in a transmission electron microscope (TEM) with a displacement control rate of 2 nm·s−1. Findings: The yield strength of HEA nanoparticles exhibits a transition from a “smaller-is-stronger” to a “smaller-is-weaker” phenomenon below a critical size of ~180 nm; The deformation mode changes from homogeneous to heterogeneous with decreasing particle size; The work-hardening ability deteriorates significantly below the critical size; The compositional heterogeneity leads to a variation in local stacking-fault energy (SFE) and lattice friction; The critical size for the transition is influenced by the spatial correlation length of compositional heterogeneity. Mechanism: The compositional heterogeneity 'roughens' the landscape for dislocation motion, leading to a variation in local SFE and lattice friction, which in turn affects the mechanical properties. Limitations: The experimental results are limited to a specific alloy composition and processing route. Future work: Further studies are needed to explore the effect of compositional heterogeneity on the mechanical properties of HEAs with different alloy compositions and processing routes. Quote: "compositional heterogeneity plays an important role in affecting the mechanical properties of HEAs"
